Test the seal moisture probe and alarm output as permitted by the manufacturer procedure without lifting the pump
List the pumps due from the asset register and confirm seal probe alarm history for each station before the route

Run timed drawdown tests on each pump and calculate the firm capacity with the largest pump out of service
Check force main pressure at peak pumping against the original readings for signs of added friction or air binding

Assemble the year results for each program against its targets, including the overflow summary and the audit results
Issue the review and plan to management and file them with the CMOM annual update so the record reads as one story
Identify the reaches and stations where outcomes did not improve despite the work done and list the evidence for each
Set next year priorities from the risk evidence: repeat overflow locations, worst condition grades, and capacity limited reaches

Extract blockage, complaint, and repeat cleaning history from the work order system for the last three years
Issue the program with monthly targets, the hotspot list, and the completion measures the supervisor will report
Rank sections into hotspot, high risk, and routine groups using blockage history, pipe age, material, and grease or root evidence
Sequence the routes by sewershed so downstream sections are cleaned before upstream sections in the same system
Set a cleaning frequency for each group and calculate the total length to be cleaned in the year

tasks.explanation: History and risk set the frequencies, and measured production rates turn length into a crew plan that can actually be finished. Downstream first sequencing stops cleaned debris from being pushed into dirty pipe, and monthly targets make slippage visible early.

Schedule the first two visits at the new interval and brief the crew on the capture and disposal requirements for grease
Review both blockage reports, the CCTV record, and the grease volumes removed at each cleaning for the section
Set a trial interval short enough that the heaviest deposit seen cannot rebuild to a blockage before the next visit
After two visits, compare the deposit found with the earlier visits and confirm or adjust the interval with the supervisor

tasks.explanation: The interval is set from the deposit growth actually observed, not from a standard table. Source inspections run in parallel because cleaning alone never wins against an uncontrolled grease source, and the trial is reviewed on evidence.

Separate lost time into causes such as buried manholes, equipment faults, weather, and traffic control delays
Reassign this week routes so the highest risk overdue sections are covered first
Record the review decisions and the revised targets in the program tracking sheet
Pull the completed work orders and compare metres cleaned, sections completed, and debris volumes with the weekly target

tasks.explanation: Production is reviewed as completed risk reduction, not just metres. Lost time is assigned to causes so the same delay is not accepted week after week, and overdue high risk sections are recovered first.

Run the grease cutting pass at the marked sections, working in short retrieves so grease is captured, not pushed ahead
Run the rotary root cutter only at the marked root joints, slowly, with continuous vacuum capture of cut roots
Vacuum the loosened material at the downstream manhole and confirm the invert is clear before any cutting pass
Review the CCTV record and mark the chainages and severity of roots, grit depth, and grease before choosing equipment
Start with a standard cleaning nozzle at the pressure set for concrete pipe to remove grit and loose debris

tasks.explanation: Each tool is used in the order that protects the pipe and the downstream system: bulk cleaning first, then grease, then cutting only where roots are proven. Cutting into a dirty pipe wastes the cutter and spreads roots downstream.

Confirm the tank load and the approved disposal location and route before leaving the last work site
Complete the work order entries for debris volumes by section and file the disposal record with the program file
At the decant area, drain free liquid back to the sanitary system only as permitted by the site procedure
Obtain and keep the disposal record showing date, volume estimate, and receiving site

tasks.explanation: Decanting is done only where permitted, because grit liquid returned at the wrong point re-enters the system it was removed from. The disposal record closes the legal chain for the material, and a washed, inspected truck starts the next shift ready.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual root control cycle for clay sewers in a mature tree lined district.

Rank the district sections by blockage history and CCTV root severity and confirm which sections are approved for chemical treatment
Review blockage calls in the district after one season and adjust the section list and cycle length in the program file
Schedule mechanical cutting first on sections with heavy root masses that would block chemical contact with fine roots
Record treated chainages, product used, and sections cut, and set the CCTV re-inspection date for the worst sections
Notify affected residents and the downstream treatment contact of the treatment dates as required by the product procedure

tasks.explanation: Heavy masses are cut first because chemical treatment works on fine regrowth, not on a root ball. Notification and exact chainage records protect residents and the treatment plant, and the cycle is adjusted on blockage results, not on the calendar alone.

tasks.prompt: Order the escalation when a cleaned grease section reblocks within one month.

Check the upstream food service grease interceptors for overdue maintenance through the grease program contact
Restore flow first with jetting and vacuum capture and confirm both affected services are draining
Compare the CCTV findings with the cleaning record, including passes made, nozzle used, and debris volume removed
Set the corrective action, such as a much shorter interval, a different nozzle program, or a repair work order, with the supervisor

tasks.explanation: Flow restoration comes first, but a one month reblock is a program failure that needs a cause, not just another cleaning. CCTV in the same window separates regrowth from a structural trap or an incomplete clean, and each cause has a different fix.

Sequence in house or contractor cleaning so each section is cleaned shortly before its survey date, not weeks ahead
Pass the survey crew the cleaning records, known access problems, and any sections that could not be cleaned to standard
Close the coordination with a list of sections surveyed, sections deferred, and the reasons, filed with the contract record
Confirm the survey sections, the required cleaning standard, and the survey start dates from the contract documents

Brief crews on continuous water circulation, hose draining, and truck freeze protection steps for each shift
Review the winter route list and defer sections that can safely wait while keeping grease hotspots and known freeze prone sections
Confirm heated water supply points, hydrant condition, and the route for locating and clearing snow covered manholes

tasks.prompt: Order a quality audit of completed cleaning work using a CCTV sample.

Confirm the pipe is cleaned to the survey standard and arrange flow control if the depth would hide the invert
Run the survey at a steady speed, stopping and panning at every defect, joint of interest, and service connection

Verify the survey header data, chainages, and video quality are complete before grading begins
Assign severity grades using the utility grading guide and note where image quality limits the grade confidence
Rank the sections by worst defect and by overall grade and list the sections needing rehabilitation assessment

Advise the owner of the findings through the supervisor, including which portion is their responsibility, in writing
Confirm the mainline is cleaned and the launch camera can pass, and notify the property owner of the inspection timing

Accept conforming sections into the asset system and update the condition grades in the asset register
Confirm defect records use the standard terms and grades and that chainages match the video counter at sampled defects

Confirm the lined section is cleaned, laterals are reinstated, and flow is normal before the camera enters

Decide with the supervisor whether the road stays closed and whether excavation, grouting, or monitoring is the next step
Set up at the nearest sound manholes and inspect toward the depression from the safer end first

Confirm flow depth and velocity are within the equipment limits and arrange the work for the low flow window
Record a full rotation inspection of each manhole wall, benching, and the pipe ends visible from the chamber
Note the limits of the inspection clearly, including the length not seen and the reason, in the survey record

At the first manhole, set up traffic control and atmosphere testing and confirm the section was cleaned to standard
Log defects in standard terms during the survey and photograph any defect that may need urgent action
Hand the day surveys, urgent defects, and any unsurveyed sections with reasons to the supervisor at shift end
Review the day sections, previous defects, and access notes and load the correct camera, crawler, and cable lengths

Set up traffic control, ventilation, and atmosphere testing at both head chambers and confirm rescue arrangements for the entry classified work
Run the camera through the isolated barrel and record sediment depth, joint condition, and any deformation with chainages

tasks.prompt: Order the installation of a temporary area velocity flow monitor in a trunk manhole.

Schedule the first data download and battery check within two weeks and record the study end date in the program file
Set up traffic control, ventilation, and atmosphere testing and confirm the entry classification for the installation work
Photograph the installation, record sensor height and pipe dimensions in the site file, and confirm data is logging before leaving
Install the sensor band or mount at the invert, level and secure it, and route the cable so it cannot catch debris

tasks.explanation: Site hydraulics decide data quality before any electronics are installed. Manual check readings at installation catch a bad sensor offset on day one instead of after six weeks, and the site file lets a different crew service the monitor correctly.

tasks.prompt: Order the deployment of rain gauges for a rainfall dependent inflow study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: three sewershed basins will be compared, and each basin needs rainfall data that matches its flow monitors.

cards.label: Level and secure each gauge, set its clock to match the flow logger clocks, and record its location and exposure in the site file
At study end, pair each basin flow record with its gauge record and file the combined data set for analysis
Download rain data on the same visits as the flow data so rainfall and flow records cover identical periods
Place one gauge in or near each study basin, clear of buildings and trees that would shelter or drip into the gauge
Check each gauge against a manual rain measurement at the first significant rainfall and note any difference
Flag dry gauge periods, tipping faults, or frozen gauge gaps in the data file as they are found, not at study end

tasks.explanation: Rainfall and flow are only comparable when clocks, periods, and locations match. Early checks against manual readings catch a faulty gauge while the study can still be saved, and data gaps are flagged honestly for the analysis.

tasks.prompt: Order a night flow analysis to estimate infiltration in a residential basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dry weather period, the basin flow monitor has four weeks of clean data, and the analysis is done in the office.

cards.label: Compare the result with the basin ranking values used by the utility and flag the basin if it exceeds the action level
Subtract the estimated legitimate night use allowance given for the basin from the average minimum flow
Extract the minimum hourly flows between 2 a.m. and 5 a.m. for each night and average the stable nights
Express the remaining flow as the estimated groundwater infiltration for the basin and note the assumptions used
File the analysis sheet with the data references and pass flagged basins to the source detection program
Confirm the analysis nights had no rainfall in the previous 48 hours using the study rain gauge record

tasks.explanation: Night flow only means infiltration after rain influenced nights and legitimate use are removed. Stating the allowance and assumptions lets another analyst reproduce the number, and flagged basins move directly into source detection.

tasks.prompt: Order the comparison and ranking of flow monitoring basins for an inflow and infiltration program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: six basins have completed eight week studies with paired rain gauges, and capital must target the worst basins first.

cards.label: Issue the ranking report with the evidence for each basin and the recommended next step and budget year
Check the top ranked basins for data quality problems, such as surcharge at the monitor or gauge gaps, before accepting the rank
Match each top basin to the next investigation step, such as smoke testing, CCTV, or manhole sealing, based on which response dominates
Rank the basins by infiltration estimate and by rainfall dependent response in two separate lists
Assemble dry weather and wet weather flow summaries for each basin using the same measures and the same study rules
Calculate each basin wet weather peaking response against its own dry weather average so basins of different sizes compare fairly

tasks.explanation: Dry and wet responses are ranked separately because infiltration and inflow have different fixes. Normalizing each basin against its own dry weather flow keeps big basins from always winning, and data quality is checked before money follows the ranking.

tasks.prompt: Order a smoke testing day in a basin flagged for rainfall dependent inflow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the basin response rises within an hour of rain, suggesting direct connections, and residents were notified last week.

cards.label: Introduce smoke section by section and walk the surface marking every emergence point with flags, photos, and addresses
Record each defect source, such as a broken cleanout cap, a connected roof leader, or a cracked lateral at the surface, by type
Confirm resident notification is complete and list properties with special conditions, such as roof leaders already known or indoor traps that may be dry
Compile the source list into the basin file with photos and issue property notices and repair work orders through the supervisor
Set up the blower at the start manhole with traffic control and atmosphere testing and seal the section as the equipment requires
Pour water into dry traps in notified buildings if smoke enters indoors and record the address for follow up

tasks.explanation: Smoke testing only works on notified streets, because unexplained smoke in homes creates alarm and false emergency calls. Every emergence point is recorded by type and address the same day, since a flag without a record finds nothing later.

tasks.prompt: Order dye testing to confirm suspected cross connections found by smoke testing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: three properties showed smoke at roof leaders or yard drains, and dye testing will confirm which drains reach the sanitary sewer.

cards.label: Test a control fixture known to be sanitary connected to confirm the observation method is working
Schedule the tests with the property owners and confirm which fixture or drain will be tested at each property
Issue the results to the supervisor for property correction notices and update the basin source inventory
Introduce dye with a measured flush of water at one source at a time while an observer watches the downstream sanitary manhole
Classify each source as confirmed connected, not connected, or inconclusive with the reason recorded
Record whether dye appears, the travel time, and the strength of the colour for each tested source

tasks.explanation: One source is tested at a time so dye in the manhole can be tied to a single drain. The control test protects the whole day, because a method fault would otherwise turn real connections into false negatives.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet weather manhole inflow survey during a spring rain event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crews will check 40 manholes in a high response basin while rain is falling, looking for cover and frame inflow sources.

cards.label: At each manhole, observe the cover, vent holes, and frame seal for ponded water entering and listen for inflow before opening
Rank the sources by estimated rate and add the top sources to the sealing and rehabilitation work plan
Estimate each source rate in the standard terms and mark manholes needing seals, inserts, or frame repairs on the route list
Brief crews on the route, the rating terms for weeping, dripping, and running leaks, and the rule not to open covers in fast traffic without control
Where safe, open the cover and observe and photograph joint and connection leaks with the asset number recorded
Return the completed route sheets the same day and enter the sources into the basin inventory before the next rain

tasks.explanation: Inflow sources are only visible while it rains, so ratings use one standard language across crews. Sources are entered and ranked before the next event, turning a wet day of observations into a repair list instead of a memory.

tasks.prompt: Order the data download and validation visit for a temporary flow monitor at week three.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the monitor is mid study, battery and data quality must be confirmed before the wettest forecast period.

cards.label: Record the visit, readings, and any data flags in the site file so the final analysis can exclude bad periods honestly
Plot the downloaded flows against the rain gauge record and flag any period where flow does not respond as expected
Compare the logged depth with a manual depth reading and check the sensor for debris fouling or movement
Clean the sensor, replace the battery if the voltage is below the study threshold, and confirm logging has restarted
Confirm the remaining study duration and the retrieval date with the program coordinator before leaving the site
Download the data on site and confirm the record is continuous with no gaps since installation

tasks.explanation: Mid study validation saves studies: a fouled sensor found at week three costs days of data, while the same fault found at retrieval costs the whole study. Flags are recorded at the visit so the analyst is not left guessing which periods to trust.

tasks.prompt: Order the effectiveness monitoring after an inflow and infiltration reduction project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 2 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a basin had manhole sealing, lateral repairs, and two cross connections removed last year, and the utility must show whether flows fell.

cards.label: File the effectiveness report in the basin record and recommend whether the next basin should use the same repair mix
Compare dry weather infiltration and storm response between the two periods using the same calculation method
Report the change with its data limits, including any development growth in the basin during the project period
Select post project storms of similar depth to the pre project storms used in the original analysis
Retrieve the pre project flow and rainfall records for the basin and confirm the monitor location can be reoccupied exactly
Install the monitor at the same site with the same sensor setup and record for a comparable season and duration

tasks.explanation: Effectiveness claims fail when the second study measures something different from the first. Same site, same method, and matched storms make the comparison fair, and growth in the basin is declared so a real reduction is not hidden or invented.
